name: Material and fee split, contingency and VAT on the summary sheet
name_hu: Anyag és díj bontás, tartalékkeret és ÁFA a főösszesítőn
review_status: Derived from Hungarian workbooks in production use. The structure below states what those files state.
description: What makes a Hungarian bill Hungarian is that every priced line is quoted twice: once as material and once as fee, meaning labour and plant. The two are totalled separately per sub-chapter, per chapter and on the cover, and the client compares tenderers on both columns rather than on the sum alone. A bill whose split does not reconcile with its own rates is not a formatting problem: it is two different answers to the question the client asked.

line_level.invariant: material unit price + fee unit price = the line's unit rate
line_level.note: Not every line carries both halves. Design fees, permits and site management are fee only and a supply-only line is material only, so the invariant is about the sum, never about both being present.

summary_cascade: Nettó anyag összesen and Nettó díj összesen, per chapter
Tartalékkeret, a contingency percentage on that subtotal
ÁFA, at the rate the statute prescribes for the work

currency.note: The forint is quoted in whole units. Two decimals on a Hungarian bill are a conversion artefact, not a price.
